title: Go language specification: Defer statements
inspection: Official language specification; relevant section read
finding: Function-exit defer stack, argument evaluation and named result semantics.
implication: Defines the source-language contract, not evidence that a translator violates it.

title: Rust Reference: Destructors
finding: Rust cleanup follows drop scopes and ownership operations.
implication: A syntactic block-to-block rewrite needs a cleanup-timing argument.

title: Rust standard library: std::fs::File
implication: A named Go result that observes Close errors cannot be justified by File Drop alone; sync_all is not established as an exact Close-error replacement.

title: Go os.Exit
finding: Exit terminates without executing deferred functions.
implication: Exclude abrupt process exit from an initial normal-return proof.

title: golang.org/x/tools/go/ssa
inspection: Official API; Defer and instruction documentation read
finding: SSA has Defer and RunDefers instructions and source positions.
implication: Use an established typed IR; SSA itself does not prove resource obligations.

title: go/packages and ssautil
inspection: Official API signatures read; packages documentation also consulted
finding: AllPackages consumes loaded packages and constructs an SSA program.
implication: Select packages.LoadAllSyntax and SSA for the compiler-backed prototype; compilation pending.

title: Go2Rust repository
inspection: Current README read; code checkout unavailable
finding: Documents conservative translation, wrapped representations and several defer features. The self-hosted behavior gate is not fully passing.
implication: Do not infer a general resource-cleanup bug from a self-hosting caveat; measure this corpus on a pinned revision.

title: Rustygo repository (KarpelesLab)
inspection: Current README read; code checkout unavailable
finding: Documents Go SSA input, a tracing GC runtime, defer support and Linux-only file/socket layer.
implication: Retained GC is an architectural choice, not evidence of incorrect cleanup. Linux is the sensible first file-benchmark platform.

title: Zhang et al. Scalable, Validated Code Translation of Entire Projects using Large Language Models. PLDI 2025.
inspection: Paper abstract and relevant design passages read
finding: Oxidizer uses feature mappings and type checks with execution-based I/O validation; reports 73% of functions validated on its evaluation.
implication: A function-level I/O result is not RescFlow resource-event accuracy or a universal equivalence proof.

title: Shadab et al. Inference of Resource Management Specifications. OOPSLA 2023.
finding: Infers resource specifications in Java/C#; reports 85.5% recovery of manually written annotations.
implication: Motivates ownership/obligation summaries; that percentage is not expected Go analysis recall.

title: Zhang et al. Ownership Guided C to Rust Translation. 2023.
finding: Crown infers ownership for C pointers and uses it for Rust translation.
implication: Ownership information is useful but does not itself encode Go defer timing.

title: Chen, Coughlin and Bond. &inator: Correct, Precise C-to-Rust Interface Translation. 2026.
finding: Constraint-based interfaces combine semantic and borrowing requirements.
implication: Use explicit proof obligations and conservative abstention; do not claim its C guarantees extend to Go cleanup.

title: Zhang et al. Validated Code Translation for Projects with External Libraries. 2026.
finding: Combines API mapping with public-API adapters for opaque library types in Go-to-Rust validation.
implication: Directly relevant to os.File and later database handles; add API-level event observations rather than comparing raw IR lifetimes.

title: Malakar et al. Repairing Leaks in Resource Wrappers. ASE 2025.
inspection: Preprint abstract plus ASE proceedings metadata verified
finding: Addresses wrapper resources and field containment in leak repair.
implication: The proposal calls this a preprint; a 2025 ASE publication is now documented. Wrapper fields deserve explicit analysis.

title: Wang et al. Mostly Automatic Translation of Language Interpreters from C to Safe Rust. 2026.
finding: Reboot reports stronger results on provided tests than on separate validation tests.
implication: Reserve held-out cases; do not treat passing the authored suite as general correctness.

title: Okhravi et al. TRACTOR Benchmark for Evaluating C to Rust Translators. 2026.
finding: Separates correctness, safety, idiomaticity and performance in a translation benchmark.
implication: Keep those dimensions distinct; relevant evaluation precedent, not a Go baseline.

title: The Go Authors. A Guide to the Go Garbage Collector
inspection: Official guide search retrieval; background only
finding: Discusses memory-management tradeoffs and resource cleanup context.
implication: Do not convert workload-specific migration stories into a universal Rust speed or leak-elimination claim.
